questions.question: Two angles on a straight line are x and 2x + 30. Write an equation with its reason, solve it, and state both angles with a check.
questions.expected_answer: x + 2x + 30 = 180 (angles on a str line), so 3x + 30 = 180, 3x = 150 and x = 50. The angles are 50 degrees and 2(50) + 30, which is 130 degrees. Check: 50 + 130 is 180.

questions.question: Two straight lines cross. One angle is 3x − 10 and the angle vertically opposite it is 2x + 20. Find x and all four angles, giving reasons, and explain why vertically opposite angles are equal.
questions.expected_answer: 3x − 10 = 2x + 20 (vert opp angles), so x = 30 and the two opposite angles are each 80 degrees. The other two angles are each 180 − 80, which is 100 degrees (angles on a str line). Vertically opposite angles are equal because each is on a straight line with the same neighbouring angle: a + b = 180 and b + c = 180, so a and c both equal 180 − b.

questions.question: Parallel lines AB and CD are cut by a transversal and one angle at the top crossing is 125 degrees. Give the sizes of its corresponding, alternate and co-interior partners with reasons, and name the shapes used to spot each pair.
questions.expected_answer: Corresponding partner: 125 degrees (corresp angles, AB ∥ CD), spotted with an F shape. Alternate partner: 125 degrees (alt angles, AB ∥ CD), spotted with a Z or N shape. Co-interior partner: 180 − 125, which is 55 degrees (co-int angles, AB ∥ CD), spotted with a C or U shape. Only co-interior angles add to 180; the other two pairs are equal.
